_comment: HAND-COMPUTED expectations for probes/widgets/scrollbar/Main.as. Never regenerate these by running the probe -- in particular the two bar colours are the values the widget writes, not samples of its output.

_derivation.root: column, align-items flex-start, padding 20, gap 10, size [320,200] -> root (0,0,320,200), content starts at (20,20).
_derivation.sv1: First child, size [200,80] -> (20,20,200,80). Vertical by default (Style.flexDirection is null unless set, and the widget/engine read 'row' only when explicitly asked), three 80px bands -> content 240 tall, so maxOffsetY = 240 - 80 = 160.
_derivation.bands: b1/b2/b3 are each [200,80] in the viewport's column: y = 0, 80, 160 locally -> stage 20, 100, 180. Their LAYOUT rects do not move when the view scrolls (scrollRect slides pixels, it does not re-solve), which is why b2/b3 are asserted at y=100/180 even though only b1 is on screen at rest.
_derivation.sv2: Second child, y = 20 + 80 + 10 = 110, size [200,40] and flexDirection 'row' -> (20,110,200,40). Its content is the 600x40 strip -> maxOffsetX = 400, maxOffsetY = 0.
_derivation.strip: row child at the viewport origin -> (20,110,600,40); r1 is the first cell -> (20,110,100,40).
_derivation.bars: Thickness 10, inset 2. sv1 overflows vertically only, so the vertical track is the right 10px of the viewport, local x 190..200 (stage 210..220), and it spans the FULL 80px height because there is no horizontal bar to make room for. Thumb length = track * view/(view+max) = 80*80/240 = 26.667, drawn inset 2 on every side -> local (192,2,6,22.667) -> stage x 212..218, y 22..44.667. So (215,30) is the thumb and (215,90) is bare track (below 44.667).
_derivation.sv2_bars: sv2's horizontal track is the bottom 10px of the viewport, local y 30..40 (stage 140..150), 200 wide (no vertical bar to give up its corner). Thumb length = 200*200/600 = 66.667 -> drawn local (2,32,62.667,6) -> stage x 22..84.667, y 142..148. (30,145) is the thumb, (150,145) is track beyond it.

points.sv1_band1: (120,30) is viewport-local (100,10); at offset 0 that is content row 10, inside b1 -> #EE1111.
points.sv1_thumb: (215,30) is viewport-local (195,10): x is the middle of the 6px-wide thumb, y is inside 2..24.667 -> the resting thumb colour #B9C2D0.
points.sv1_track: (215,90) is viewport-local (195,70): same bar, below the thumb and away from its rounded caps -> the track colour #E8EDF5.
points.sv1_no_hbar: (170,95) is viewport-local (150,75) -- right where a horizontal track would be painted (local y 70..80) -- and it still shows b1 (#EE1111). A bar on an axis with maxOffset 0 is the lie this pins. x=150 rather than 190 because the vertical bar covers the right 10px.
points.sv2_cell1: (30,115) is sv2-local (10,5), i.e. content x=10 -> r1 #EE1111.
points.sv2_thumb: (30,145) is sv2-local (10,35): the horizontal thumb spans local x 2..64.667, y 32..38 -> #B9C2D0.
points.sv2_no_vbar: (215,115) is sv2-local (195,5), where a vertical track would be, and it still shows the content: content x=195 -> r2 #11EE11.

_derivation.behaviour: Steady state first: contentH 240 / maxOffsetY 160 for sv1 and contentW 600 / maxOffsetX 400 / maxOffsetY 0 for sv2. Then one wheel notch (wheelStep 20) over sv1 moves offsetY to 20 and NOT offsetX, and slides b2 into the window at local y=70 (content row 90). Then dragging the vertical thumb 15px down must give offsetY = 15 * 160 / (80 - 26.667) = 45 -- the thumb tracks the pointer 1:1, so the free travel is the FULL thumb length, not the 4px-shorter drawn rect; the drag must also move the thumb on screen (it leaves y 2..24.667 and the old spot turns into track) and the content (local y=70 now shows content row 115 = b2). Clamps: 9999 -> 160 on sv1 (thumb at the track's end, local 53.333..80) and 9999 -> 400 on sv2. The horizontal fallback: a wheel over sv2 (maxOffsetY 0) moves offsetX to 20 and the pixels slide with it (stage x=110 is local 90, i.e. content x=110 = r2). No momentum, no elastic overscroll: those are absent on purpose.
